overview: The Medford School Committee approved a new district incident report policy, adopted the 2018–2019 school calendar, and reviewed the Fine Arts preliminary budget and high school graduation rates. The committee also referred school facility rental policies to the Committee of the Whole while mandating police details for outside weekend rentals.

items.title: Approval of Bills and Transfer of Funds
items.summary: Approved the payment of bills and transfer of funds.

items.title: Approval of Payrolls and Reporting Motion
items.summary: Tabled a motion to require administration to provide an ongoing electronic spreadsheet detailing employee payrolls and backup data.

items.title: Report of the Secretary
items.summary: Accepted and placed on file the secretary's expenditure report regarding invoice processing and account description updates.

items.title: Community Participation: Special Education Parent Advisory Council
items.summary: Referred a request from CPAC leadership to create a dedicated school committee subcommittee focused on special education and high-needs students.

items.title: Commendation of Anthony Petrelis and Camp Finances
items.summary: Commended elementary teacher Anthony Petrelis for keeping children calm during a school security sweep at vacation camp, and voted to request financial records for Community Schools camp programs.

items.title: Report on Elementary Response to Intervention
items.summary: Accepted a report on the rollout of the first-grade Response to Intervention literacy pilot and upcoming assessment tool adjustments.

items.title: McGlynn Middle School Grade 7 Overnight Field Trip
items.summary: Approved an overnight environmental science field trip to the University of Rhode Island for seventh-grade students.

items.title: Medford Vocational Technical High School DECA Field Trip
items.summary: Approved an overnight trip for students to participate in the DECA state competition in Boston.

items.title: Community Outreach Subcommittee Announcement
items.summary: Announced that the Community Relations Subcommittee will hold a meeting at the senior center on March 9.

items.title: Incident Report Policy
items.summary: Approved a revised district incident report policy detailing mandatory police notifications, administrative reporting, and public communication protocols.

items.title: Medford High School Graduation and Dropout Rates
items.summary: Received a state report showing Medford High School's graduation rate increased to 90.3 percent while its dropout rate decreased to 2.7 percent.

items.title: Fine Arts Department Pre-Budget Report
items.summary: Accepted the Fine Arts Department report requesting level funding with slight increases for piano tuning and band transportation.

items.title: 2018–2019 School Calendar Approval
items.summary: Approved the 2018–2019 school calendar draft with the March professional development day removed to be scheduled at a later date.

items.title: Brooks School ExxonMobil Grant
items.summary: Approved two $500 grant checks from ExxonMobil affiliates for Brooks School math and science materials.

items.title: Community Participation: Middle School Administration
items.summary: Heard parent concerns and comments from Principal Paul D'Alleva regarding administrative staffing support across the middle schools.

items.title: Resolutions of Condolence
items.summary: Adopted condolence resolutions for the families of Irene Anestis, Tilly Fodey, and Joe Small.

items.title: School Facility Rentals and Security Review
items.summary: Referred school building rental policies to the Committee of the Whole while requiring police details for outside weekend rentals in the interim, and agreed to close the superintendent search survey.

items.title: Executive Session
items.summary: Voted to convene in executive session to discuss employee negotiations, security strategies, and an employee complaint.
